title: Hollywood Directors & Creators
tagline: Men and women who got the camera and kept the vision. Ownership of the story is ownership of the culture.

entries.name: Spike Lee
entries.claim: The NYU grad whose thesis film won a student Academy Award, then funded She's Gotta Have It with credit cards and independent money when Hollywood said no.
entries.receipts: She's Gotta Have It (1986): shot for $175,000, grossed $7 million+ — the film that proved Black stories could be profitable, opening the studio door for a generation. Do the Right Thing (1989): still taught in film schools. He wrote NYU's Kickstarter-funded film. Over 30 features, an Academy Honorary Award, and the first-ever commercial for a feature film shot on an iPhone (a Nike commercial on a phone). He has his own production company (40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks) — ownership from day one.
entries.the_transfer: Spike funded his first feature on credit cards because the studios passed. He then built his OWN production company and has kept it for 40 years — 40 Acres and a Mule. That's the FED-EDU move: when the platform turns you down, build your own with the tools you have. Your GitHub org IS your 40 Acres. The repo is the film. Ship it yourself.

entries.name: Ryan Coogler
entries.claim: The USC grad whose first feature (Fruitvale Station) was funded by a grant and kindness, then directed Black Panther ($1.3 billion) before turning 32.
entries.receipts: Fruitvale Station (2013): budget under $1M, won Sundance Grand Jury Prize and Cannes. Creed (2015): revived a 40-year franchise. Black Panther (2018): $1.3 billion worldwide — one of the highest-grossing films ever made, with a predominantly Black cast, shot in Atlanta. Sinners (2025): his own original IP, self-financed through his Proximity Media, which he owns.
entries.the_transfer: Coogler's arc is the roadmap: small personal film → studio trust → biggest film in the world → OWN original IP (Sinners, self-financed). The FED-EDU mirror: first $150 client site → first $500 multi-page build → your own SaaS product. Same ladder, different industry. And note the middle step: he did franchise work (Creed) to EARN the trust for the original work. Take the franchise work. Build the trust. Then build your own.

entries.name: Ava DuVernay
entries.self_note: Sister on the matrix — directors' chairs don't check gender, and any matrix of Black filmmaking that skips Ava is incomplete.
entries.claim: The publicist who taught herself directing at 32, built her own distribution company (ARRAY) when the industry had no room for Black women directors, and became the first Black woman to direct a $100M film.
entries.receipts: Selma (2014): first Black woman to direct a Best Picture nominee. 13th (2016): Netflix, Oscar-nominated. A Wrinkle in Time (2018): $100M+ budget — first Black woman to direct a nine-figure studio film. Founder of ARRAY Alliance and the ARRAY Crew jobs database for below-the-line film workers of color. Her first film cost $6,000.
entries.the_transfer: Ava's first film cost $6,000. Her last ones cost $100M+. The in-between was NOT talent alone — it was building her OWN distribution when nobody would distribute her: ARRAY. When the gatekeepers say no, the answer isn't always 'try harder' — sometimes it's 'build the infrastructure the gatekeeper refused to build.' Your own GitHub org, your own PWA, your own DM system (fed-comm-dm) — that's ARRAY energy. Build the road yourself and others can drive on it too.

entries.name: Jordan Peele
entries.claim: The comedian who left a hit sketch show at the top, taught himself horror film grammar from scratch, and became the first Black writer to win the Original Screenplay Oscar.
entries.receipts: Get Out (2017): $4.5M budget, $255M gross, Oscar for Best Original Screenplay — the first Black screenwriter ever to win it. Us (2019): $71M opening weekend, the highest for an original horror film. Nope (2022): shot on IMAX. Monkeypaw Productions — he owns it. He started as a comedian on MADtv and Key & Peele — total career pivot at 33.
entries.the_transfer: Jordan Peele switched careers at the top of his old one — left Key & Peele at its peak to direct horror, a genre he was told Black directors 'don't do.' Career pivot at 33+ is the second-chance story in this repo: the brother starting tech at 30, 40, 50 after another life — Peele proves the pivot works. Your past skill COMES WITH you: his comedy timing IS his horror timing. Your street knowledge IS your product sense. Nothing is wasted.

entries.name: John Singleton
entries.claim: The USC student whose senior thesis script became Boyz n the Hood — the youngest person and first Black filmmaker ever nominated for the Best Director Oscar.
entries.pro_tips: Singleton wrote Boyz n the Hood as his film school thesis. He wrote what he knew. The studio gave him the money because nobody else was telling that story.
entries.receipts: Boyz n the Hood (1991): Best Director and Best Original Screenplay Oscar nominations at 24 — youngest Best Director nominee ever and the first Black man nominated in that category. Poetic Justice, Higher Learning, the 2 Fast franchise entry, and the Snowfall series about the era he grew up in. He was posthumously honored by the Directors Guild.
entries.the_transfer: Singleton wrote the story only HE could write, at 24, and the Oscars followed. Your block is your moat — the product ideas nobody else can see because they didn't grow up where you grew up. The hustle apps you'll build from this repo — league stats, clip tools, community DMs — exist because YOU saw the need on your block. The gatekeepers call it niche. The market calls it underserved. Write what you know. That's the advantage.

entries.name: Barry Jenkins
entries.claim: The Florida State film grad from Liberty City who waited eight years between his first feature and Moonlight — and won the Best Picture Oscar over La La Land in the most famous envelope mix-up in history.
entries.receipts: Medicine for Melancholy (2008): micro-budget first feature. Then eight years of commercials and HBO work while the craft sharpened. Moonlight (2016): Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay Oscars, shot for $1.5M, defeating La La Land on the biggest stage in Hollywood. If Beale Street Could Talk (2018): adapted James Baldwin. The Underground Railroad series and Mufasa for Disney.
entries.the_transfer: Eight years between features. EIGHT. The brother who feels 'behind' — Jenkins waited eight years between projects and won Best Picture on the next one. There is no schedule. There is no behind. There is only the next project and the craft getting sharper in the silence. Your 'gap years' were Jenkins years. Keep working in the dark. The work compounds even when nobody's clapping.
